evidence.quote: DeepSeek is developing its own AI chips to reduce its reliance on products from Nvidia and Huawei
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek is developing its own AI chips, citing three sources familiar with the plans (Reuters), designed for inference.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (three unnamed sources)
evidence.original_who: Reuters, citing three sources familiar with the plans

evidence.quote: Huawei has expanded its domestic market share and now controls around half of China's AI chip market, which is valued at approximately US$50 billion.
evidence.one_line: Huawei controls about half of China's AI chip market, valued at about US$50 billion.
evidence.speaker: idnfinancials.com (media)

evidence.quote: "Nvidia's position in China is effectively at zero and will remain that way."
evidence.one_line: Analyst Richard Windsor of Radio Free Mobile says Nvidia's China position is effectively zero and will stay that way.
evidence.speaker: Richard Windsor, Radio Free Mobile

evidence.quote: OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, called Jalapeno, last month in collaboration with Broadcom
evidence.one_line: OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, Jalapeno, with Broadcom, in the prior month.
evidence.speaker: idnfinancials.com (media)

evidence.quote: Reuters previously reported that the company was preparing its first funding round worth US$7 billion, with a valuation of between US$52 billion and US$59 billion
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek was reportedly preparing a first funding round of US$7 billion at a US$52–59 billion valuation.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (reported earlier)

evidence.quote: DeepSeek V4 model, which had been optimised for Huawei Ascend chips, while Huawei revealed that training for the V4-Flash model also used Ascend processors.
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek launched its V4 model in April, optimised for Huawei Ascend chips; Huawei said V4-Flash training also used Ascend processors.
evidence.speaker: DeepSeek and Huawei (as reported)
